title: What Power Quietly Does to a Leader
excerpt: Power rarely announces itself. This week it created distance, built echoes, bent boundaries and blurred the mission. You may lead the room, but you remain a man under God.
author: TheWrkShop Team
seo_title: What Power Quietly Does to a Leader: Weekend 4-3-2-1 | TheWrkShop
seo_description: Four Scriptures, three insights, two questions and one action step on how power creates distance, echoes and exceptions, and how to stay a man under God.
body_html: What Power Quietly Does to a Leader
What distance, echoes, exceptions, loyalty and the mission taught us this week

This week we looked at five things power can quietly do to a leader. It creates distance. It builds an echo chamber. It whispers, “This is different.” It draws loyalty that belongs to Christ. And it lets the mission become the man.
None of it gets announced. Nobody holds a meeting and decides to deceive you. Nobody announces, “I am becoming entitled.” Power changes the environment, and slowly relationships change.
If you lead anyone, at work, at home or in the church, remember this: you may lead the room, but you remain a man under God.

One-Minute Win of the Week
Before your next decision, take 60 seconds and ask: “Would I believe this was appropriate if someone else did it?”

A leader finishes his Monday meeting and asks, “Everybody good?” Every head nods. He walks out confident. Down the hall, two people from that same meeting are finally saying what they didn’t say inside it. Same room. Same plan. He just experienced a different organization than everyone else.
“He is to read it all the days of his life so that he may learn to revere the LORD his God…. and not consider himself better than his fellow Israelites….”
Insight: God kept Israel’s kings under His Word so the man everybody bows to would remember he is still a man under God.
Gem: Power creates elevation. Scripture creates remembrance.

“So the king of Israel brought together the prophets, about four hundred men, and asked them, ‘Shall I go to war against Ramoth Gilead, or shall I refrain?’ ‘Go,’ they answered…. But Jehoshaphat asked, ‘Is there no longer a prophet of the LORD here whom we can inquire of?’”
Insight: Four hundred voices said, “Go,” but consensus can be what remains after dissent becomes too expensive.
Gem: Agreement is not always evidence of alignment.
“In the spring, at the time when kings go off to war…. David remained in Jerusalem.”
Insight: The story opens with a powerful king increasingly able to arrange reality around himself.
Gem: Power increases your ability to turn desire into access.
“Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly together in front of the rock and Moses said to them, ‘Listen, you rebels, must we bring you water out of this rock?’”
Insight: “Must we….” shows how easy it is for long-term leadership to blur God’s work with my identity.
Gem: God invites us into His work. He does not hand us ownership of it.
• When disagreement becomes expensive, agreement becomes unreliable. Wise leaders don’t only ask, “Who agrees?” They also ask, “Who sees this differently?”
• No human leader gets the allegiance that belongs to Christ. Biblical loyalty does not require moral blindness: I can honor you without worshiping you.
• You can be important without being ultimate. The kingdom existed before us, and the kingdom will continue after us.
• Who knows the man behind the authority?
• Do I have access that my character has not learned to govern?
Get your idea tested: Invite a trusted person to argue the other side. Tell them, “Don’t protect my idea. Test it.” Then resist the urge to win. Listen.
Nobody builds an echo chamber on purpose. Watch the progression:
Now the leader says, “Everybody I trust agrees with me.” But perhaps the system gradually changed who was allowed to remain trusted.
Gem: What truth might have left the room before I noticed?

Prayer
Father, keep authority from distorting how I see myself. Protect me from surrounding myself with echoes. Give me people who love truth more than proximity. Keep blessing from becoming permission. Keep access from becoming indulgence. Never let me demand from people what belongs only to Jesus. Forgive me where stewardship has become ownership. This belongs to You. I am a steward, not the owner. In Jesus’ name, amen.

Declaration
My position is an assignment, not my identity. I may lead the room, but I remain a man under God.
Challenge: Before each big decision this week, imagine an empty chair and ask, “Who is not in this room?” Then go hear from that person before you decide.
Invitation: If this hit you where you are, share it with a friend. Let’s build men of faith, together.
